# Historical: APY, TVL, share-price and asset-price time series
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/historical

> Index of the v2 historical endpoints (oldest-first time series, Unix-seconds windows, perPage up to 20000) for vault APY, TVL, share price and asset prices, with credit costs and links to every endpoint page.

This section lists the v2 endpoints that return time series for one vault (APY, TVL, share price) or one asset (USD price). Use them for charts, backtests and realised-return calculations. For the current value, use [Detailed vaults](/api-reference/detailed-vaults) instead; it is cheaper.

All requests go to `https://api.vaults.fyi` with the header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. Without a key, v2 endpoints return 402 (an [x402](/ai-agents/x402) payment challenge); beta, alpha and NRT endpoints need an API key. APY values are decimal fractions net of fees (`0.0315` = 3.15%); token amounts are integer strings in base units; timestamps are Unix seconds. See [Conventions](/api-reference/conventions).

## Endpoints

| Endpoint | Use it when | Required inputs | Credits |
| - | - | - | - |
| [`GET /v2/historical/{network}/{vaultId}`](/api-reference/historical/get-vault-historical-data) | Get APY, TVL and share price together for one vault over time. Use a single-series endpoint if you need only one (cheaper). | Path: `network`, `vaultId` | 3 + 3 per data point |
| [`GET /v2/historical/{network}/{vaultId}/apy`](/api-reference/historical/get-historical-apy) | APY series for one vault, `apy.{base,reward,total}` over the trailing `apyInterval`, sampled every `granularity`. | Path: `network`, `vaultId` | 1 + 1 per data point |
| [`GET /v2/historical/{network}/{vaultId}/tvl`](/api-reference/historical/get-historical-tvl) | TVL series for one vault (`tvl.usd`, `tvl.native`). | Path: `network`, `vaultId` | 1 + 1 per data point |
| [`GET /v2/historical/{network}/{vaultId}/sharePrice`](/api-reference/historical/get-historical-share-price) | Share-price series for one vault; use it to compute realised returns between two dates. | Path: `network`, `vaultId` | 1 + 1 per data point |
| [`GET /v2/historical/asset-prices/{network}/{assetAddress}`](/api-reference/historical/get-historical-asset-prices) | USD price series for one token address on one network. | Path: `network`, `assetAddress` | 1 + 1 per data point |

Credits are from [Credits](/plans/credits): base cost per call, plus a per-item cost where shown. Pay-as-you-go is $0.002 per credit. A "data point" is one element of `data[]`. Example: 30 days at the default `granularity=1hour` is 720 points, so `/v2/historical/{network}/{vaultId}` costs 3 + 3 × 720 = 2,163 credits. With `granularity=1day` it is 30 points, or 93 credits.

## Query parameters and defaults

| Parameter | Default | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `fromTimestamp` | `0` | Unix **seconds**. The default starts at the beginning of history (USDC asset prices start in 2022). Milliseconds return 400. |
| `toTimestamp` | now | Unix seconds. `fromTimestamp > toTimestamp` returns 200 with no data. |
| `granularity` | `1hour` | `1hour`, `1day`, `1week`. |
| `apyInterval` | `7day` | Trailing window each APY point is computed over: `1day`, `7day`, `30day`, `90day`. |
| `page`, `perPage` | `0`, `50` | `perPage` up to 20000. |

- Results are ordered **oldest first**. To get the most recent points, set `fromTimestamp` close to now instead of reading page 0.
- `nextPage` is omitted on the last page. There is no total count.
- APY points are `{base, reward, total}` decimal fractions, net of fees. `tvl.usd` is a USD string, `tvl.native` is base units, and `sharePrice` is a number (underlying assets per one whole share).

## Example

```bash
curl -H "x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY" \
  "https://api.vaults.fyi/v2/historical/base/0xbeeff2490FEffa212faC2f6553682C219E6a8845/apy?fromTimestamp=1792540800&toTimestamp=1792713600&granularity=1day&apyInterval=7day&perPage=5"
```

Response, captured 2026-10-23 (complete):

```json
{
  "itemsOnPage": 3,
  "data": [
    { "timestamp": 1792540800, "blockNumber": "52875727", "apy": { "base": 0.0315, "reward": 0, "total": 0.0315 } },
    { "timestamp": 1792627200, "blockNumber": "52918927", "apy": { "base": 0.0315, "reward": 0, "total": 0.0315 } },
    { "timestamp": 1792713600, "blockNumber": "52962127", "apy": { "base": 0.0315, "reward": 0, "total": 0.0315 } }
  ]
}
```

`nextPage` is absent, so this is the last page.

# Get one vault's APY, TVL and share-price history
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/historical/get-vault-historical-data

> Returns a combined time series for one vault: per point `timestamp` (Unix seconds), `blockNumber`, `apy` {base, reward, total} as decimal fractions net of fees over the trailing `apyInterval` window, `tvl` {usd, native} and `sharePrice`. Ordered oldest first; `fromTimestamp` defaults to 0 (start of history), so pass a Unix-seconds start for a recent window. `granularity` 1hour|1day|1week (default 1hour). Use the /apy, /tvl or /sharePrice variants when you need one series: they cost 1 credit per point instead of 3. Paginated: `perPage` up to 20000. Cost: 3 credits + 3 per data point. Docs: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/historical/get-vault-historical-data.

## Request

`GET https://api.vaults.fyi/v2/historical/{network}/{vaultId}`

- Auth: header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. Without a key this v2 endpoint returns 402 (x402 payment challenge); an invalid key returns 401.
- Credits: 3 credits + 3 per data point ([Credits](/plans/credits)).
- Stability: stable (v2) ([Versioning](/api-reference/versioning)).
- operationId: `getHistoricalData`. Section: [Historical](/api-reference/historical).

## Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| `network` | path | string: one of 44 values (`mainnet`, `optimism`, `arbitrum`, …; full list in the OpenAPI block) | yes | — | Network name (e.g. `base`, `mainnet`) or CAIP-2 ID (e.g. `eip155:8453`). Bare chain IDs (`8453`) and `ethereum` are rejected with 400. List all with GET /v2/networks. |
| `vaultId` | path | string | yes | — | Vault identifier: `vaultId` from GET /v2/vaults or /v2/detailed-vaults, an opaque string. Either the vault contract address, or `<address>-<descriptor>` for vaults that share one contract (e.g. `0x559756d476D5ed4533edC3Ac98E5A9468176378c-25`): copy it, don't derive it from `address`. The address part is case-insensitive; pass the descriptor exactly as returned. A vault that migrates to a new contract gets a new vaultId. Must belong to `{network}`; otherwise 400 'Vault ... on network ... not found'. Non-vault strings return 400 'not a valid vault id'. |
| `page` | query | integer (≥ 0) | no | `0` | Zero-based page index (default 0). Request the response's `nextPage` until that key is absent (it is omitted, never null, on the last page); a page past the end returns 200 with empty `data`. There is no total count. |
| `perPage` | query | integer (> 0, ≤ 20000) | no | `50` | Items per page, 1-20000 (default 50). 0 or more than 20000 returns 400. Every returned item is billed (see x-credits); request only what you need. |
| `apyInterval` | query | string: `1day`, `7day`, `30day`, `90day` | no | `"7day"` | Trailing window used for the returned APY values and for ranking: 1day, 7day, 30day or 90day (default 7day). APY values are decimal fractions net of fees. |
| `granularity` | query | string: `1hour`, `1day`, `1week` | no | `"1hour"` | Spacing between returned points: 1hour, 1day or 1week (default 1hour). Points align to even intervals from Unix epoch 0. Each point is billed, so coarser granularity is cheaper. |
| `fromTimestamp` | query | integer (≥ 0, ≤ 99999999999) | no | `0` | Start of the window, Unix seconds (not milliseconds; values >= 1e11 return 400). Default 0 = start of history, so page 0 holds the OLDEST data: pass a recent timestamp for recent data. Results are oldest first. |
| `toTimestamp` | query | integer (≥ 0, ≤ 99999999999) | no | — | End of the window, Unix seconds (not milliseconds). Default: now. A value before fromTimestamp returns 200 with empty data. |

## Example request

```bash
curl -sS 'https://api.vaults.fyi/v2/historical/base/0xbeeff2490FEffa212faC2f6553682C219E6a8845?granularity=1day&perPage=3' \
  -H "x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY"
```

# Get one vault's share-price history
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/historical/get-historical-share-price

> Returns share-price history for one vault: `sharePrice` = underlying assets per one whole share (a float ratio, not base units), with `timestamp` (Unix seconds) and `blockNumber`, oldest first from `fromTimestamp` (default 0). Use two points to compute realised returns between dates: return = sharePrice_end / sharePrice_start - 1. Cost: 1 credit + 1 per data point. Docs: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/historical/get-historical-share-price.

## Request

`GET https://api.vaults.fyi/v2/historical/{network}/{vaultId}/sharePrice`

- Auth: header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. Without a key this v2 endpoint returns 402 (x402 payment challenge); an invalid key returns 401.
- Credits: 1 credit + 1 per data point ([Credits](/plans/credits)).
- Stability: stable (v2) ([Versioning](/api-reference/versioning)).
- operationId: `getHistoricalSharePrice`. Section: [Historical](/api-reference/historical).

## Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| `network` | path | string: one of 44 values (`mainnet`, `optimism`, `arbitrum`, …; full list in the OpenAPI block) | yes | — | Network name (e.g. `base`, `mainnet`) or CAIP-2 ID (e.g. `eip155:8453`). Bare chain IDs (`8453`) and `ethereum` are rejected with 400. List all with GET /v2/networks. |
| `vaultId` | path | string | yes | — | Vault identifier: `vaultId` from GET /v2/vaults or /v2/detailed-vaults, an opaque string. Either the vault contract address, or `<address>-<descriptor>` for vaults that share one contract (e.g. `0x559756d476D5ed4533edC3Ac98E5A9468176378c-25`): copy it, don't derive it from `address`. The address part is case-insensitive; pass the descriptor exactly as returned. A vault that migrates to a new contract gets a new vaultId. Must belong to `{network}`; otherwise 400 'Vault ... on network ... not found'. Non-vault strings return 400 'not a valid vault id'. |
| `page` | query | integer (≥ 0) | no | `0` | Zero-based page index (default 0). Request the response's `nextPage` until that key is absent (it is omitted, never null, on the last page); a page past the end returns 200 with empty `data`. There is no total count. |
| `perPage` | query | integer (> 0, ≤ 20000) | no | `50` | Items per page, 1-20000 (default 50). 0 or more than 20000 returns 400. Every returned item is billed (see x-credits); request only what you need. |
| `apyInterval` | query | string: `1day`, `7day`, `30day`, `90day` | no | `"7day"` | Accepted for consistency with the other historical endpoints; has no effect on TVL or share-price values. Values: 1day, 7day, 30day, 90day (default 7day). |
| `granularity` | query | string: `1hour`, `1day`, `1week` | no | `"1hour"` | Spacing between returned points: 1hour, 1day or 1week (default 1hour). Points align to even intervals from Unix epoch 0. Each point is billed, so coarser granularity is cheaper. |
| `fromTimestamp` | query | integer (≥ 0, ≤ 99999999999) | no | `0` | Start of the window, Unix seconds (not milliseconds; values >= 1e11 return 400). Default 0 = start of history, so page 0 holds the OLDEST data: pass a recent timestamp for recent data. Results are oldest first. |
| `toTimestamp` | query | integer (≥ 0, ≤ 99999999999) | no | — | End of the window, Unix seconds (not milliseconds). Default: now. A value before fromTimestamp returns 200 with empty data. |

## Example request

```bash
  -H "x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY"
```

# Benchmarks: USD and ETH benchmark APY
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/benchmarks

> Index of the v2 benchmark endpoints: current and historical vaults.fyi benchmark APY for USD (code=usd) or ETH (code=eth) strategies on a network, 3 credits per call, with links to both endpoint pages.

This section lists the v2 endpoints for the vaults.fyi benchmark rates: a reference APY for USD and ETH strategies on a network. Use them to tell whether a vault's yield beats the market baseline. The methodology is on [Benchmark rates](/methodology/benchmark-rates).

All requests go to `https://api.vaults.fyi` with the header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. Without a key, v2 endpoints return 402 (an [x402](/ai-agents/x402) payment challenge); beta, alpha and NRT endpoints need an API key. APY values are decimal fractions net of fees (`0.0315` = 3.15%); token amounts are integer strings in base units; timestamps are Unix seconds. See [Conventions](/api-reference/conventions).

## Endpoints

| Endpoint | Use it when | Required inputs | Credits |
| - | - | - | - |
| [`GET /v2/benchmarks/{network}`](/api-reference/benchmarks/get-benchmark-rate) | Current vaults.fyi benchmark APY for USD (`code=usd`) or ETH (`code=eth`) strategies on a network. `code` is required. | Path: `network`; Query: `code` | 3 |
| [`GET /v2/historical-benchmarks/{network}`](/api-reference/benchmarks/get-historical-benchmarks) | Benchmark APY history for `code=usd` or `code=eth`. | Path: `network`; Query: `code` | 3 + 3 per data point |

Credits are from [Credits](/plans/credits): base cost per call, plus a per-item cost where shown. Pay-as-you-go is $0.002 per credit.

## Things to know

- `code` is **required** and must be `usd` or `eth`. `code=btc` or a missing `code` returns 400.
- The response `apy` has windows `1day`, `7day`, `30day`, `90day`, each `{base, reward, total}` as a decimal fraction. The spec marks `apy` as nullable.
- `timestamp` is Unix seconds.
- Historical benchmarks are oldest first, `fromTimestamp` defaults to 0, and `perPage` goes up to 20000. Windows before the first data point return empty pages.

## Example

```bash
curl -H "x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY" "https://api.vaults.fyi/v2/benchmarks/base?code=usd"
```

Response, captured 2026-10-23 (complete):

```json
{
  "apy": {
    "1day":  { "base": 0.0407, "reward": 0, "total": 0.0407 },
    "7day":  { "base": 0.0407, "reward": 0, "total": 0.0407 },
    "30day": { "base": 0.0395, "reward": 0, "total": 0.0395 },
    "90day": { "base": 0.0382, "reward": 0, "total": 0.0382 }
  },
  "timestamp": 1792713600
}
```

The 7-day USD benchmark on Base was 4.07%.

Related: [Historical](/api-reference/historical), [Conventions](/api-reference/conventions), [Errors](/api-reference/errors).


# Get the current USD or ETH benchmark APY on a network
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/benchmarks/get-benchmark-rate

> Returns the current vaults.fyi benchmark APY for USD (`code=usd`) or ETH (`code=eth`) strategies on a network: `apy` windows {base, reward, total} as decimal fractions and `timestamp` (Unix seconds). `code` is required (400 without it). `apy` can be null. Benchmarks are computed once per day (UTC) as a TVL-weighted average of the 5 largest featured USD or ETH vaults (each over $1M TVL) on the network; a network needs at least 3 qualifying vaults to have a benchmark. Cost: 3 credits. Docs: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/benchmarks/get-benchmark-rate.

## Request

`GET https://api.vaults.fyi/v2/benchmarks/{network}`

- Auth: header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. Without a key this v2 endpoint returns 402 (x402 payment challenge); an invalid key returns 401.
- Credits: 3 credits ([Credits](/plans/credits)).
- Stability: stable (v2) ([Versioning](/api-reference/versioning)).
- operationId: `getBenchmark`. Section: [Benchmarks](/api-reference/benchmarks).

## Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| `network` | path | string: one of 44 values (`mainnet`, `optimism`, `arbitrum`, …; full list in the OpenAPI block) | yes | — | Network name (e.g. `base`, `mainnet`) or CAIP-2 ID (e.g. `eip155:8453`). Bare chain IDs (`8453`) and `ethereum` are rejected with 400. List all with GET /v2/networks. |
| `code` | query | string: `usd`, `eth` | yes | — | Benchmark: `usd` (USD-denominated strategies) or `eth` (ETH-denominated strategies). Required; missing or other values return 400. |

## Example request

```bash
curl -sS 'https://api.vaults.fyi/v2/benchmarks/base?code=usd' \
  -H "x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY"
```

## Response (200)

Success: get the current USD or ETH benchmark APY on a network

Response headers: `x-ratelimit-limit`, `x-ratelimit-remaining`, `x-ratelimit-reset` (see [Errors, rate limits and retries](/api-reference/errors)).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| - | - | - | - |
| `timestamp` | integer | yes | Timestamp of the benchmark data point. Unix seconds. |
| `apy` | object, nullable | yes | Benchmark APY by window, each {base, reward, total} as decimal fractions. Can be null when no benchmark value is available. Fields: `1day`, `7day`, `30day`, `90day`. |

# Portfolio: positions, idle assets, returns and deposit suggestions
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/portfolio

> Index of the v2 wallet endpoints (positions, idle assets, best vault, best deposit options, total returns, events) with their 4-network default scope, position-size semantics, credit costs and links to every endpoint page.

This section lists the v2 endpoints that read one wallet: its vault positions, idle (undeposited) tokens, suggested deposits, lifetime returns and event history. Use them for portfolio views and deposit recommendations. Nothing here moves funds; to build transactions, use [Transactions](/api-reference/transactions).

All requests go to `https://api.vaults.fyi` with the header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. Without a key, v2 endpoints return 402 (an [x402](/ai-agents/x402) payment challenge); beta, alpha and NRT endpoints need an API key. APY values are decimal fractions net of fees (`0.0315` = 3.15%); token amounts are integer strings in base units; timestamps are Unix seconds. See [Conventions](/api-reference/conventions).

## Endpoints

| Endpoint | Use it when | Required inputs | Credits |
| - | - | - | - |
| [`GET /v2/portfolio/positions/{userAddress}`](/api-reference/portfolio/list-portfolio-positions) | List a wallet's vault positions. Position size is `asset.positionValueInAsset` or `lpToken.balanceUsd`, not `asset.balanceUsd`. Defaults: 4 networks, `minTvl=100000`. | Path: `userAddress` | 5 |
| [`GET /v2/portfolio/positions/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}`](/api-reference/portfolio/get-portfolio-position) | Get one wallet's position in one known vault (cheaper than listing). | Path: `userAddress`, `network`, `vaultId` | 1 |
| [`GET /v2/portfolio/idle-assets/{userAddress}`](/api-reference/portfolio/list-idle-assets) | List a wallet's tokens that are not deposited in a vault. Sort with `sortDirection` (not `sortOrder`). | Path: `userAddress` | 5 |
| [`GET /v2/portfolio/best-deposit-options/{userAddress}`](/api-reference/portfolio/get-best-deposit-options) | For each asset the wallet holds, get up to `maxVaultsPerAsset` (default 3) vaults ranked by APY. Defaults: `onlyAppFeatured=true`, `allowVaultsWithWarnings=false`. | Path: `userAddress` | 1 + 2 per vault returned |
| [`GET /v2/portfolio/best-vault/{userAddress}`](/api-reference/portfolio/get-best-vault) | Get the single best vault for the asset the wallet holds most of. Can return `isTransactional: false`; pass `onlyTransactional=true` before building a deposit. | Path: `userAddress` | 2 |
| [`GET /v2/portfolio/total-returns/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}`](/api-reference/portfolio/get-total-returns) | Lifetime returns of a wallet in one vault (`returnsNative`, base units). | Path: `userAddress`, `network`, `vaultId` | 1 |
| [`GET /v2/portfolio/events/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}`](/api-reference/portfolio/list-position-events) | All deposit and withdrawal events of a wallet in one vault. Not paginated; `items` is the total count. | Path: `userAddress`, `network`, `vaultId` | 3 |

Credits are from [Credits](/plans/credits): base cost per call, plus a per-item cost where shown. Pay-as-you-go is $0.002 per credit.

## Things to know

- **Default network scope.** `positions`, `idle-assets`, `best-vault` and `best-deposit-options` cover only base, mainnet, arbitrum and optimism unless you pass `allowedNetworks` (one repeated key per network). A wallet's positions on other networks are silently omitted.
- **Default `minTvl=100000`** on `positions`, `best-vault` and `best-deposit-options` hides positions in vaults under $100k TVL.
- **Position size is not `asset.balanceUsd`.** In positions, `asset.balanceNative` and `asset.balanceUsd` are the wallet's idle balance of the underlying token, repeated on every position in that asset. The position is `asset.positionValueInAsset` (base units) or `lpToken.balanceUsd`. Summing `asset.balanceUsd` over-counts. See [Conventions → Positions](/api-reference/conventions#positions-wallet-balance-vs-position-size).
- **Best-vault defaults differ** from list endpoints: `onlyAppFeatured=true` and `allowVaultsWithWarnings=false`. `best-vault` can still return a vault with `isTransactional: false`; pass `onlyTransactional=true` if you will build a deposit.
- **Idle assets** sort with `sortBy` + `sortDirection` (not `sortOrder`), with default `minUsdAssetValueThreshold=0.5`.
- **Not paginated.** These endpoints return `{data, errors}` with everything in one response. `events` returns `{asset, lpToken, data, items}`, where `items` is the total count.
- `userAddress` must be `0x` + 40 hex characters. ENS names return 400. Addresses are case-insensitive.
- Path order is user, then network, then vault: `/v2/portfolio/positions/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}`.

## Example

```bash
# Default scope: base, mainnet, arbitrum, optimism. Add allowedNetworks=<name> (repeated) for others.
curl -H "x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY" \
  "https://api.vaults.fyi/v2/portfolio/positions/0xd8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA96045"
```

# List a wallet's vault positions
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/portfolio/list-portfolio-positions

> Lists a wallet's vault positions with APY and TVL context. Position size is `asset.positionValueInAsset` (underlying base units) or `lpToken.balanceUsd`. `asset.balanceNative` / `asset.balanceUsd` are the wallet's idle balance of the underlying token, repeated on every position in that asset: never sum them as position value. Defaults: allowedNetworks = base, mainnet, arbitrum, optimism ONLY; minTvl = 100000 (also hides your positions in smaller vaults; pass minTvl=0); minUsdAssetValueThreshold = 1 USD; apyInterval = 7day. Not paginated: returns {data, errors}. To rank positions by size, sort by `lpToken.balanceUsd` client-side. Use /v2/portfolio/positions/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId} for one known vault (1 credit). Cost: 5 credits. Docs: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/portfolio/list-portfolio-positions.

## Request

`GET https://api.vaults.fyi/v2/portfolio/positions/{userAddress}`

- Auth: header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. Without a key this v2 endpoint returns 402 (x402 payment challenge); an invalid key returns 401.
- Credits: 5 credits ([Credits](/plans/credits)).
- Stability: stable (v2) ([Versioning](/api-reference/versioning)).
- operationId: `listPortfolioPositions`. Section: [Portfolio](/api-reference/portfolio).

## Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| `userAddress` | path | string, pattern `^0x[a-fA-F0-9]{40}$` | yes | — | Wallet address whose data is returned. EVM address: 0x + 40 hex characters (checksum optional). ENS names such as vitalik.eth are not resolved (400). |
| `allowedAssets` | query | array of string | no | — | Underlying assets to include, by ticker symbol (case-insensitive, e.g. `USDC`); token addresses are NOT accepted and are echoed in `errors.unsupportedAssets`. Repeat the key once per value (`allowedAssets=a&allowedAssets=b`). A comma-separated value (`allowedAssets=a,b`) is NOT split: it is treated as one unknown value and silently returns empty results. |
| `disallowedAssets` | query | array of string | no | — | Underlying assets to exclude, by ticker symbol. Ignored when `allowedAssets` is set. Repeat the key once per value (`disallowedAssets=a&disallowedAssets=b`). A comma-separated value (`disallowedAssets=a,b`) is NOT split: it is treated as one unknown value and silently returns empty results. |
| `allowedProtocols` | query | array of string | no | — | Protocols to include: protocol `name` or exact `protocolId` from GET /v2/protocols. A name matches EVERY protocolId with that name: `morpho` = `morpho-metamorpho` (Morpho V1 / MetaMorpho vaults) + `morpho-v2` (Morpho V2 vaults) + `morpho-market` (borrow markets); `aave` matches 8 protocolIds. Use the protocolId to select one product, e.g. `morpho-metamorpho` for Morpho V1 only, or `aave-collateral vault-v3` for Aave v3 (it contains a space: send `aave-collateral%20vault-v3`). Guessed IDs such as `aave-v3` return 200 with empty `data` and the value in `errors.unsupportedProtocols`. Repeat the key once per value (`allowedProtocols=a&allowedProtocols=b`). A comma-separated value (`allowedProtocols=a,b`) is NOT split: it is treated as one unknown value and silently returns empty results. |
| `disallowedProtocols` | query | array of string | no | — | Protocols to exclude, by `name` or `protocolId` from GET /v2/protocols. Ignored when `allowedProtocols` is set (the allow-list wins). Repeat the key once per value (`disallowedProtocols=a&disallowedProtocols=b`). A comma-separated value (`disallowedProtocols=a,b`) is NOT split: it is treated as one unknown value and silently returns empty results. |
| `minTvl` | query | integer (≥ 0) | no | `100000` | Minimum vault TVL in whole USD (integer; 1000.5 returns 400). Default 100000: vaults under $100k are hidden unless you pass minTvl=0 (this also hides the wallet's positions in smaller vaults). |
| `minVaultScore` | query | number (≥ 0) | no | — | Minimum Reputation Score (0-100, compared with `score.vaultScore`). Check `score.vaultScore` client-side if you need a strict threshold. |
| `onlyTransactional` | query | boolean | no | — | true = only vaults that /v2/transactions can build payloads for (`isTransactional: true`). Pass true before recommending a vault you will deposit into. Literal `true`/`false` only. |
| `onlyAppFeatured` | query | boolean | no | — | true = only vaults featured in app.vaults.fyi. Literal `true`/`false` only. |
| `allowCorrupted` | query | boolean | no | `false` | true = include vaults flagged as corrupted (unreliable data). Default false. |
| `allowVaultsWithWarnings` | query | boolean | no | `true` | Include vaults that have active `warnings` (e.g. bad debt, compromised keys). Default true: warned vaults ARE returned; pass false, or inspect `warnings` and `flags`, before recommending a vault. |
| `allowedNetworks` | query | array of string: one of 44 values (`mainnet`, `optimism`, `arbitrum`, …; full list in the OpenAPI block) | no | `["base", "mainnet", "arbitrum", "optimism"]` | Networks to include, by name (`base`) or CAIP-2 (`eip155:8453`). Default when omitted: base, mainnet, arbitrum, optimism ONLY; data on every other network is silently excluded, so list each network you need. Unknown values are echoed in `errors.unsupportedNetworks` with HTTP 200. Some names returned by GET /v2/networks currently have no indexed vaults (observed 2026-10-24: `swellchain`); list endpoints echo them in `errors.unsupportedNetworks` while still returning rows for the other networks, so treat that echo as a warning, not a failure. For a complete pull, take network names from GET /v2/vaults (see https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/conventions). Repeat the key once per value (`allowedNetworks=a&allowedNetworks=b`). A comma-separated value (`allowedNetworks=a,b`) is NOT split: it is treated as one unknown value and silently returns empty results. |
| `disallowedNetworks` | query | array of string: one of 44 values (`mainnet`, `optimism`, `arbitrum`, …; full list in the OpenAPI block) | no | — | Networks to exclude (name or CAIP-2). Ignored when `allowedNetworks` is set. When `allowedNetworks` is omitted, passing `disallowedNetworks` REPLACES the default network scope: every network except the listed ones is searched (verified 2026-10-24: `disallowedNetworks=mainnet` alone returned vaults on 20 networks). Repeat the key once per value (`disallowedNetworks=a&disallowedNetworks=b`). A comma-separated value (`disallowedNetworks=a,b`) is NOT split: it is treated as one unknown value and silently returns empty results. |
| `maxTvl` | query | integer | no | — | Maximum TVL in whole USD (integer). |
| `maxApy` | query | number | no | — | Maximum APY (in decimal) of the vaults to be included. |
| `minApy` | query | number | no | — | Minimum APY (in decimal) of the vaults to be included. |
| `tags` | query | array of string | no | — | Tags from GET /v2/tags to include, e.g. `Liquid Staking`. Use exact tag names: matching is case-insensitive, but abbreviations such as `lst` return 200 with empty data. Repeat the key once per value (`tags=a&tags=b`). A comma-separated value (`tags=a,b`) is NOT split: it is treated as one unknown value and silently returns empty results. |
| `curators` | query | array of string | no | — | Curator `name`s from GET /v2/curators to include, exactly as listed (full names such as `Steakhouse Financial`; a partial name such as `Steakhouse` matches nothing). Unknown names return empty results with no `errors` echo, so resolve the name from /v2/curators first. Repeat the key once per value (`curators=a&curators=b`). A comma-separated value (`curators=a,b`) is NOT split: it is treated as one unknown value and silently returns empty results. |
| `sortOrder` | query | string: `asc`, `desc` | no | `"asc"` | Sort direction, `asc` or `desc` (lowercase; `DESC` returns 400). Default `asc`: pass `desc` to get the highest values first. |
| `sortBy` | query | string: `balanceUsd`, `tvl`, `apy1Day`, `apy7Day`, `apy30Day`, `apy90Day` | no | — | Sort key: `balanceUsd` (position/balance value in USD), `tvl` (TVL in USD), `apy1Day` (1-day total APY), `apy7Day` (7-day total APY), `apy30Day` (30-day total APY), `apy90Day` (90-day total APY). Case-sensitive. Without sortBy the order is unspecified (not ranked): always pass sortBy and sortOrder. To rank positions by size, sort by `lpToken.balanceUsd` client-side. |
| `apyInterval` | query | string: `1day`, `7day`, `30day`, `90day` | no | `"7day"` | Trailing window used for the returned APY values and for ranking: 1day, 7day, 30day or 90day (default 7day). APY values are decimal fractions net of fees. |
| `minUsdAssetValueThreshold` | query | number (≥ 0) | no | `1` | Ignore holdings worth less than this many USD (default 1). |

# Get a wallet's position in one vault
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/portfolio/get-portfolio-position

> Returns one wallet's position in one vault (same object as an item of the positions list, same caveat: `asset.balanceNative`/`balanceUsd` are the wallet's idle balance of the underlying, not the position; position size is `asset.positionValueInAsset` or `lpToken.balanceUsd`). Cheaper than listing when you know network and vaultId. Cost: 1 credit. Docs: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/portfolio/get-portfolio-position.

## Request

`GET https://api.vaults.fyi/v2/portfolio/positions/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}`

- Auth: header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. Without a key this v2 endpoint returns 402 (x402 payment challenge); an invalid key returns 401.
- Credits: 1 credit ([Credits](/plans/credits)).
- Stability: stable (v2) ([Versioning](/api-reference/versioning)).
- operationId: `getPortfolioPosition`. Section: [Portfolio](/api-reference/portfolio).

## Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| `userAddress` | path | string, pattern `^0x[a-fA-F0-9]{40}$` | yes | — | Wallet address whose data is returned. EVM address: 0x + 40 hex characters (checksum optional). ENS names such as vitalik.eth are not resolved (400). |
| `network` | path | string: one of 44 values (`mainnet`, `optimism`, `arbitrum`, …; full list in the OpenAPI block) | yes | — | Network name (e.g. `base`, `mainnet`) or CAIP-2 ID (e.g. `eip155:8453`). Bare chain IDs (`8453`) and `ethereum` are rejected with 400. List all with GET /v2/networks. |
| `vaultId` | path | string | yes | — | Vault identifier: `vaultId` from GET /v2/vaults or /v2/detailed-vaults, an opaque string. Either the vault contract address, or `<address>-<descriptor>` for vaults that share one contract (e.g. `0x559756d476D5ed4533edC3Ac98E5A9468176378c-25`): copy it, don't derive it from `address`. The address part is case-insensitive; pass the descriptor exactly as returned. A vault that migrates to a new contract gets a new vaultId. Must belong to `{network}`; otherwise 400 'Vault ... on network ... not found'. Non-vault strings return 400 'not a valid vault id'. |
| `apyInterval` | query | string: `1day`, `7day`, `30day`, `90day` | no | `"7day"` | Trailing window used for the returned APY values and for ranking: 1day, 7day, 30day or 90day (default 7day). APY values are decimal fractions net of fees. |

## Example request

```bash
curl -sS 'https://api.vaults.fyi/v2/portfolio/positions/0xd8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA96045/mainnet/0xae7ab96520DE3A18E5e111B5EaAb095312D7fE84?apyInterval=30day' \
  -H "x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY"
```

Success: get a wallet's position in one vault

Response headers: `x-ratelimit-limit`, `x-ratelimit-remaining`, `x-ratelimit-reset` (see [Errors, rate limits and retries](/api-reference/errors)).

# List a wallet's undeposited token balances

Docs: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/portfolio/list-idle-assets.

Default when omitted: base, mainnet, arbitrum, optimism ONLY; data on every other network is silently excluded, so list each network you need. Unknown values are echoed in `errors.unsupportedNetworks` with HTTP 200. Some names returned by GET /v2/networks currently have no indexed vaults (observed 2026-10-24: `swellchain`); list endpoints echo them in `errors.unsupportedNetworks` while still returning rows for the other networks, so treat that echo as a warning, not a failure. For a complete pull, take network names from GET /v2/vaults (see https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/conventions). Repeat the key once per value (`allowedNetworks=a&allowedNetworks=b`). A comma-separated value (`allowedNetworks=a,b`) is NOT split: it is treated as one unknown value and silently returns empty results. |
| `disallowedNetworks` | query | array of string: one of 44 values (`mainnet`, `optimism`, `arbitrum`, …; full list in the OpenAPI block) | no | — | Networks to exclude (name or CAIP-2). Ignored when `allowedNetworks` is set. When `allowedNetworks` is omitted, passing `disallowedNetworks` REPLACES the default network scope: every network except the listed ones is searched (verified 2026-10-24: `disallowedNetworks=mainnet` alone returned vaults on 20 networks). Repeat the key once per value (`disallowedNetworks=a&disallowedNetworks=b`). A comma-separated value (`disallowedNetworks=a,b`) is NOT split: it is treated as one unknown value and silently returns empty results. |

# Rank deposit options for each asset a wallet holds
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/portfolio/get-best-deposit-options

> For each asset the wallet holds (worth at least minUsdAssetValueThreshold, default 1 USD), returns up to maxVaultsPerAsset (default 3) vaults ranked by APY over apyInterval (default 7day), with projected annual USD earnings. Defaults: onlyAppFeatured=true, allowVaultsWithWarnings=false, minTvl=100000, allowedNetworks=base, mainnet, arbitrum, optimism. Use `alwaysReturnAssets` to include assets the wallet does not hold. Use after /idle-assets to suggest deposits; use /best-vault for a single answer. Cost: 1 credit + 2 per vault returned. Docs: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/portfolio/get-best-deposit-options.

## Request

`GET https://api.vaults.fyi/v2/portfolio/best-deposit-options/{userAddress}`

- Auth: header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. Without a key this v2 endpoint returns 402 (x402 payment challenge); an invalid key returns 401.
- Credits: 1 credit + 2 per vault returned ([Credits](/plans/credits)).
- Stability: stable (v2) ([Versioning](/api-reference/versioning)).
- operationId: `getBestDepositOptions`. Section: [Portfolio](/api-reference/portfolio).

## Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| `userAddress` | path | string, pattern `^0x[a-fA-F0-9]{40}$` | yes | — | Wallet address whose data is returned. EVM address: 0x + 40 hex characters (checksum optional). ENS names such as vitalik.eth are not resolved (400). |
| `allowedAssets` | query | array of string | no | — | Underlying assets to include, by ticker symbol (case-insensitive, e.g. `USDC`); token addresses are NOT accepted and are echoed in `errors.unsupportedAssets`. Repeat the key once per value (`allowedAssets=a&allowedAssets=b`). A comma-separated value (`allowedAssets=a,b`) is NOT split: it is treated as one unknown value and silently returns empty results. |

A comma-separated value (`disallowedAssets=a,b`) is NOT split: it is treated as one unknown value and silently returns empty results. |

A name matches EVERY protocolId with that name: `morpho` = `morpho-metamorpho` (Morpho V1 / MetaMorpho vaults) + `morpho-v2` (Morpho V2 vaults) + `morpho-market` (borrow markets); `aave` matches 8 protocolIds. | `disallowedNetworks` | query | array of string: one of 44 values (`mainnet`, `optimism`, `arbitrum`, …; full list in the OpenAPI block) | no | — | Networks to exclude (name or CAIP-2). Ignored when `allowedNetworks` is set. When `allowedNetworks` is omitted, passing `disallowedNetworks` REPLACES the default network scope: every network except the listed ones is searched (verified 2026-10-24: `disallowedNetworks=mainnet` alone returned vaults on 20 networks). Repeat the key once per value (`disallowedNetworks=a&disallowedNetworks=b`). A comma-separated value (`disallowedNetworks=a,b`) is NOT split: it is treated as one unknown value and silently returns empty results. |
| `apyInterval` | query | string: `1day`, `7day`, `30day`, `90day` | no | `"7day"` | Trailing window used for the returned APY values and for ranking: 1day, 7day, 30day or 90day (default 7day). APY values are decimal fractions net of fees. |
| `minApy` | query | number (≥ 0) | no | — | Minimum APY (in decimal) of the vaults to be included. |
| `maxApy` | query | number | no | — | Maximum APY (in decimal) of the vaults to be included. |
| `maxTvl` | query | integer | no | — | Maximum TVL in whole USD (integer). |

# Get the single best vault for a wallet's largest asset
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/portfolio/get-best-vault

> Returns one vault recommendation for the wallet: for each asset held it picks the vault with the highest total APY over `apyInterval`, then returns the asset/vault pair with the highest projected annual earnings, plus that asset's wallet balance (`asset.balanceNative` base units, `asset.balanceUsd`). Defaults differ from list endpoints: onlyAppFeatured=true, allowVaultsWithWarnings=false, minTvl=100000, allowedNetworks=base, mainnet, arbitrum, optimism, apyInterval=7day. The result can have isTransactional=false: pass onlyTransactional=true if you will build a deposit. Use /v2/portfolio/best-deposit-options for several options per asset. Cost: 2 credits. Docs: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/portfolio/get-best-vault.

# Get a wallet's lifetime returns in one vault
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/portfolio/get-total-returns

> Returns the lifetime returns of a wallet in one vault as `returnsNative` (underlying-asset base units, integer string; can be 0 or negative) plus asset metadata. For a time window use /beta/portfolio/partial-returns. Cost: 1 credit. Docs: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/portfolio/get-total-returns.

## Request

`GET https://api.vaults.fyi/v2/portfolio/total-returns/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}`

- Auth: header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. Without a key this v2 endpoint returns 402 (x402 payment challenge); an invalid key returns 401.
- Credits: 1 credit ([Credits](/plans/credits)).
- Stability: stable (v2) ([Versioning](/api-reference/versioning)).

# Transactions: unsigned deposit, redeem and reward-claim payloads
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/transactions

> Index of the v2 transaction endpoints: context first, then unsigned ordered actions for deposit, redeem and reward claims (amounts in base units, no simulation, no balance check), with credit costs and links to every endpoint page.

This section lists the v2 endpoints that build **unsigned** EVM transactions for vault actions and reward claims. The API returns calldata only. It never signs, broadcasts, simulates or checks balances. Your app or agent must verify each payload and have the user sign it.

All requests go to `https://api.vaults.fyi` with the header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. Without a key, v2 endpoints return 402 (an [x402](/ai-agents/x402) payment challenge); beta, alpha and NRT endpoints need an API key. Amounts are integer strings in the asset's base units: 1 USDC (6 decimals) is `amount=1000000`, and `amount=1.5` returns 400.

## Endpoints

| Endpoint | Use it when | Required inputs | Credits |
| - | - | - | - |
| [`GET /v2/transactions/context/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}`](/api-reference/transactions/get-transaction-context) | Call first: which deposit/redeem steps apply, the next step, wallet balances (base units), pending requests and claimable rewards for one vault. | Path: `userAddress`, `network`, `vaultId` | 3 |
| [`GET /v2/transactions/{action}/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}`](/api-reference/transactions/get-transaction-payload) | Build **unsigned** ordered `actions[]` (e.g. approve then deposit). `amount` is a base-unit integer string; `all=true` redeems a full position. No balance check, no simulation. | Path: `action`, `userAddress`, `network`, `vaultId`; Query: `assetAddress` | 5 |
| [`GET /v2/transactions/rewards/context/{userAddress}`](/api-reference/transactions/get-rewards-context) | List claimable rewards by network; each entry has the `claimId` you pass to the claim endpoint. | Path: `userAddress` | 3 |
| [`GET /v2/transactions/rewards/claim/{userAddress}`](/api-reference/transactions/claim-rewards) | Build unsigned reward-claim transactions for `claimIds` (repeat the key per ID). | Path: `userAddress`; Query: `claimIds` | 5 |
| [`GET /v2/transactions/suffix/{userAddress}/{vaultId}`](/api-reference/transactions/get-transaction-suffix) | Get the attribution suffix for your own calldata. v2 transaction payloads already end with it. | Path: `userAddress`, `vaultId` | 1 |

Credits are from [Credits](/plans/credits): base cost per call, plus a per-item cost where shown. Pay-as-you-go is $0.002 per credit.

## Typical flow

1. `GET /v2/transactions/context/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}`: read which steps apply (`depositSteps`, `redeemSteps`), the next step, the wallet's balances (base units), any pending requests, and claimable rewards.
2. `GET /v2/transactions/{action}/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}?assetAddress=…&amount=…`: build the payload. Actions include `deposit`, `redeem`, `request-redeem`, `request-deposit`, `claim-redeem`, `claim-deposit`, `claim-rewards` and `start-redeem-cooldown`. `assetAddress` is required; use the vault's `asset.address`. Use `all=true` instead of `amount` to redeem a full position.
3. Execute `actions[]` **in order** (for example, approve and then deposit), waiting for each to confirm. Before each signature, verify `tx.chainId` matches the network, `tx.to` is the asset (for approvals) or the vault, and the amount is what the user intended.

Things to know:

- Path order is user, then network, then vault. `/v2/transactions/context/{network}/{userAddress}/{vaultId}` returns 400.
- `tx.value` is omitted on ERC-20 flows. Treat a missing `value` as `0`.
- `simulate` is deprecated and ignored. No `simulation` object is returned. Simulate client-side (for example with `eth_call`) if you need guarantees.
- There is no balance check: a deposit larger than the wallet balance still returns a payload. Compare with the context's balance first.
- Every payload's `data` already ends with your attribution suffix. Call the suffix endpoint only if you build calldata yourself. See [TVL attribution](/concepts/tvl-attribution).
- Rewards are two calls: get `claimId`s from the rewards context, then pass them as repeated `claimIds` keys to the claim endpoint.

## Example

```bash
# 1 USDC (6 decimals) into Steakhouse High Yield USDC on Base, for a read-only example wallet
curl -H "x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY" \
  "https://api.vaults.fyi/v2/transactions/deposit/0xd8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA96045/base/0xbeeff2490FEffa212faC2f6553682C219E6a8845?assetAddress=0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913&amount=1000000"
```

Response, captured 2026-10-23 (complete; calldata unchanged):

```json
{
  "currentActionIndex": 0,
  "actions": [
    {
      "name": "Approve USDC for Steakhouse High Yield USDC Edition vault",
      "tx": {
        "to": "0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913",
        "chainId": 8453,
        "data": "0x095ea7b3000000000000000000000000beeff2490feffa212fac2f6553682c219e6a884500000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000f4240"
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "Deposit USDC to Steakhouse High Yield USDC Edition vault",
      "tx": {
        "to": "0xbeeff2490FEffa212faC2f6553682C219E6a8845",
        "chainId": 8453,
        "data": "0x6e553f6500000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000f4240000000000000000000000000d8da6bf26964af9d7eed9e03e53415d37aa96045232c5f404de80be3c7ef2001de2d09ce535a2a0fffc69deb"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Two actions: approve 1 USDC (`0xf4240` = 1000000) to the vault, then deposit. Neither has a `value` field. The deposit calldata ends with the attribution suffix. The full schema is on [Get transaction payload](/api-reference/transactions/get-transaction-payload). Safety checks for agents are on [Transaction safety](/ai-agents/transaction-safety).

# Get balances and next steps before a vault transaction
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/transactions/get-transaction-context

> Call before building any vault transaction. Returns which deposit/redeem steps apply (`depositSteps`/`redeemSteps` with action names and `actionsUrl`), the step to run next (`currentDepositStep`/`currentRedeemStep`), the wallet's asset and LP-token balances (base units), pending deposit/redeem requests, claimable rewards and protocol-specific state (`vaultSpecificData`). Use it to choose `action`, check balance and `decimals`, and detect queued redemptions: a queued withdrawal is claimable when `currentRedeemStep` becomes `claim-redeem` (call its `actionsUrl`); `pendingRequests` is filled only for some protocols, and you never pass claim IDs. `depositStepsType`/`redeemStepsType` `instant` = finishes without waiting (may still be approve + deposit); `complex` = a waiting period between steps (e.g. request-redeem -> wait -> claim-redeem). Read-only. Cost: 3 credits. Docs: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/transactions/get-transaction-context.

## Request

`GET https://api.vaults.fyi/v2/transactions/context/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}`

- Auth: header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. Without a key this v2 endpoint returns 402 (x402 payment challenge); an invalid key returns 401.
- Credits: 3 credits ([Credits](/plans/credits)).
- Stability: stable (v2) ([Versioning](/api-reference/versioning)).
- operationId: `getTransactionContext`. Section: [Transactions](/api-reference/transactions).

## Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| `userAddress` | path | string, pattern `^0x[a-fA-F0-9]{40}$` | yes | — | Wallet address whose data is returned. EVM address: 0x + 40 hex characters (checksum optional). ENS names such as vitalik.eth are not resolved (400). |
| `network` | path | string: one of 44 values (`mainnet`, `optimism`, `arbitrum`, …; full list in the OpenAPI block) | yes | — | Network name (e.g. `base`, `mainnet`) or CAIP-2 ID (e.g. `eip155:8453`). Bare chain IDs (`8453`) and `ethereum` are rejected with 400. List all with GET /v2/networks. |
| `vaultId` | path | string | yes | — | Vault identifier: `vaultId` from GET /v2/vaults or /v2/detailed-vaults, an opaque string. Either the vault contract address, or `<address>-<descriptor>` for vaults that share one contract (e.g. `0x559756d476D5ed4533edC3Ac98E5A9468176378c-25`): copy it, don't derive it from `address`. The address part is case-insensitive; pass the descriptor exactly as returned. A vault that migrates to a new contract gets a new vaultId. Must belong to `{network}`; otherwise 400 'Vault ... on network ... not found'. Non-vault strings return 400 'not a valid vault id'. |

## Example request

```bash
curl -sS 'https://api.vaults.fyi/v2/transactions/context/0xd8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA96045/base/0xbeeff2490FEffa212faC2f6553682C219E6a8845' \
  -H "x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY"
```

## Response (200)

Success: get balances and next steps before a vault transaction

Response headers: `x-ratelimit-limit`, `x-ratelimit-remaining`, `x-ratelimit-reset` (see [Errors, rate limits and retries](/api-reference/errors)).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| - | - | - | - |
| `currentDepositStep` | string: `deposit`, `redeem`, `request-redeem`, `request-deposit`, `claim-redeem`, `claim-deposit`, `claim-rewards`, `start-redeem-cooldown` | yes | Name of the deposit step to execute next; matches an `action` value. |
| `currentRedeemStep` | string: `deposit`, `redeem`, `request-redeem`, `request-deposit`, `claim-redeem`, `claim-deposit`, `claim-rewards`, `start-redeem-cooldown` | yes | Name of the redeem step to execute next; matches an `action` value. |
| `childrenPositions` | array of object | yes | Positions in child vaults of this vault (nested vaults), same shape as the parent position fields. Item fields: `address`, `lpToken`, `asset`, `additionalAssets`. |
| `vaultSpecificData` | object | no | Protocol-specific transactional state (cooldowns, queued requests, KYC, fees). The shape depends on the vault's protocol: one of the anyOf variants, or absent. |
| `pendingRequests` | object | no | Queued (asynchronous) deposit and redeem requests of this wallet in this vault. `status` is `pending` or `ready` (ready = claim with claim-deposit / claim-redeem). Fields: `deposits`, `redeems`. |

# Build unsigned vault transactions (deposit, redeem, claim)
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/transactions/get-transaction-payload

> Builds UNSIGNED transactions; `tx.data` can be absent for native-token deposits and `tx.value` can be non-zero. Pass data only when present and always pass value (missing value means 0); value-only deposits have no calldata attribution suffix. One vault action: deposit, redeem, request-redeem, request-deposit, claim-redeem, claim-deposit, claim-rewards or start-redeem-cooldown. `assetAddress` is required; `amount` is an integer string in base units (deposit / request-deposit: underlying-asset base units, 1 USDC = "1000000"; redeem / request-redeem: vault-share (LP-token) base units on most vaults (ERC-4626, ERC-7540, Ethena, Veda, Compound v2), but underlying-asset base units on asset-based lending markets such as Aave v3/v4, Compound v3 and borrow-market aliases); use all=true to redeem the wallet's full share balance. For a native-ETH vault (e.g. Lido stETH) pass assetAddress=0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000: the amount is sent as `tx.value` (wei) with no approve step. Returns ordered `actions[]` (e.g. approve then deposit): sign and send them in order, waiting for each receipt, and verify `tx.to` and `tx.chainId` first. `tx.value` is present only for native-token actions (treat a missing value as 0). Nothing is submitted, no balance check is made (an amount above the wallet balance still returns 200) and nothing is simulated (`simulate` is deprecated and ignored); allowance is read only to set `currentActionIndex`, and the approve step is still returned. The actions are plain calls (`to`, `data`, `value`); if you batch them in a smart-wallet call, pass each vault call's `data` through unchanged (it carries the attribution suffix). Call /v2/transactions/context/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId} first to pick the action and read decimals. Calldata is protocol-specific: not every vault uses the ERC-4626 `deposit(uint256,address)` selector `0x6e553f65` (e.g. Sky Savings USDS uses `0x9b8d6d38` = `deposit(uint256,address,uint16)`), so verify by decoding against the target ABI or simulating with eth_call, not by matching a fixed selector list (https://docs.vaults.fyi/ai-agents/transaction-safety). Cost: 5 credits. Docs: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/transactions/get-transaction-payload.

## Request

`GET https://api.vaults.fyi/v2/transactions/{action}/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}`

- Auth: header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. Without a key this v2 endpoint returns 402 (x402 payment challenge); an invalid key returns 401.
- Credits: 5 credits ([Credits](/plans/credits)).
- Stability: stable (v2) ([Versioning](/api-reference/versioning)).
- operationId: `getTransaction`. Section: [Transactions](/api-reference/transactions).

## Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| `action` | path | string: `deposit`, `redeem`, `request-redeem`, `request-deposit`, `claim-redeem`, `claim-deposit`, `claim-rewards`, `start-redeem-cooldown` | yes | — | Vault action to build. `deposit`/`redeem` for instant vaults; queued vaults use `request-deposit`/`request-redeem`, then `claim-deposit`/`claim-redeem` once ready; `claim-rewards` claims this vault's rewards; `start-redeem-cooldown` starts a cooldown where the vault requires one. Pick the action from `depositSteps`/`redeemSteps` in /v2/transactions/context/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}. |
| `userAddress` | path | string, pattern `^0x[a-fA-F0-9]{40}$` | yes | — | Wallet that will sign and send the transaction; it is also the receiver/owner encoded in the calldata. EVM address: 0x + 40 hex characters (checksum optional). ENS names such as vitalik.eth are not resolved (400). |
| `network` | path | string: one of 44 values (`mainnet`, `optimism`, `arbitrum`, …; full list in the OpenAPI block) | yes | — | Network name (e.g. `base`, `mainnet`) or CAIP-2 ID (e.g. `eip155:8453`). Bare chain IDs (`8453`) and `ethereum` are rejected with 400. List all with GET /v2/networks. |
| `vaultId` | path | string | yes | — | Vault identifier: `vaultId` from GET /v2/vaults or /v2/detailed-vaults, an opaque string. Either the vault contract address, or `<address>-<descriptor>` for vaults that share one contract (e.g. `0x559756d476D5ed4533edC3Ac98E5A9468176378c-25`): copy it, don't derive it from `address`. The address part is case-insensitive; pass the descriptor exactly as returned. A vault that migrates to a new contract gets a new vaultId. Must belong to `{network}`; otherwise 400 'Vault ... on network ... not found'. Non-vault strings return 400 'not a valid vault id'. |
| `assetAddress` | query | string, pattern `^0x[a-fA-F0-9]{40}$` | yes | — | Underlying token you deposit or receive: the vault's `asset.address` (from the context or detailed-vault response). Required for every action. For a native-ETH vault (e.g. Lido stETH) this is the zero address 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 (the amount is then sent as `tx.value`, with no approve step); use the WETH address for WETH vaults, and don't use 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. A token the vault does not accept returns 400 'Asset ... is not investable'. |
| `simulate` | query | boolean | no | `false` | **Deprecated.** Deprecated and ignored: the server never simulates and never returns `actions[].simulation`. Simulate client-side (e.g. eth_call) before signing. |
| `amount` | query | string, pattern `^[0-9]+$` | no | — | Amount as an integer string in base units, no decimal point (`1.5` returns 400 'Expected bigint'). deposit / request-deposit: underlying-asset base units (human amount x 10^asset.decimals; 1 USDC = "1000000"). Compute it with integer/decimal math (viem parseUnits, Python Decimal); float math such as (1500.25*1e18).toString() yields "1.50025e+21", which returns 400. redeem / request-redeem: passed unchanged to the vault contract, so the unit depends on the protocol: vault SHARES in LP-token base units (10^lpToken.decimals) on most vaults (ERC-4626, ERC-7540, Ethena, Veda, Compound v2), underlying-asset base units on asset-based lending markets such as Aave v3/v4, Compound v3 and borrow-market aliases. Lido uses stETH vault-token base units. For share-unit protocols, amount = floor((assetBaseUnits / 10^asset.decimals) / sharePrice * 10^lpToken.decimals), using decimal/integer-rational math; sharePrice (asset per share) comes from NRT or the detailed vault. This is an estimate: use the on-chain previewWithdraw/conversion method for an exact asset-target exit and verify balance/rounding before signing. Send all=true to redeem the wallet's full share balance. Required for deposit, request-deposit, redeem and request-redeem (all=true can replace it for redeem / request-redeem); claim-redeem, claim-deposit, claim-rewards and start-redeem-cooldown take no amount. No balance check is made. |
| `all` | query | boolean | no | — | true = redeem / request-redeem the wallet's full share balance instead of `amount`. Only meaningful for redeem and request-redeem (other actions ignore it). Literal true/false. |

# Get the attribution calldata suffix for your API key
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/transactions/get-transaction-suffix

> Returns the hex attribution suffix (no 0x prefix) for this API key, user and vault. It is deterministic for a given API key, user address and vault, so you can cache it. Vault-call calldata from /v2/transactions/{action}/... already ends with it (don't append it again); native value-only deposits have no calldata or suffix; call this only if you build calldata yourself and want deposits attributed to your key. Generate it for the address the vault sees as the depositor (for a smart wallet, the smart-account address). Needs an API key with attribution enabled: otherwise 400 (not charged); it can't be bought keyless over x402. Cost: 1 credit. Docs: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/transactions/get-transaction-suffix.

## Request

`GET https://api.vaults.fyi/v2/transactions/suffix/{userAddress}/{vaultId}`

- Auth: header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. Without a key this v2 endpoint returns 402 (x402 payment challenge); an invalid key returns 401.
- Credits: 1 credit ([Credits](/plans/credits)).
- Stability: stable (v2) ([Versioning](/api-reference/versioning)).
- operationId: `getTransactionSuffix`. Section: [Transactions](/api-reference/transactions).

## Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| `userAddress` | path | string, pattern `^0x[a-fA-F0-9]{40}$` | yes | — | Wallet the attribution suffix is generated for. EVM address: 0x + 40 hex characters (checksum optional). ENS names such as vitalik.eth are not resolved (400). |
| `vaultId` | path | string | yes | — | Vault identifier: `vaultId` from GET /v2/vaults or /v2/detailed-vaults, an opaque string. Either the vault contract address, or `<address>-<descriptor>` for vaults that share one contract (e.g. `0x559756d476D5ed4533edC3Ac98E5A9468176378c-25`): copy it, don't derive it from `address`. The address part is case-insensitive; pass the descriptor exactly as returned. A vault that migrates to a new contract gets a new vaultId. Must belong to `{network}`; otherwise 400 'Vault ... on network ... not found'. Non-vault strings return 400 'not a valid vault id'. |

## Example request

```bash
curl -sS 'https://api.vaults.fyi/v2/transactions/suffix/0xd8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA96045/0xbeeff2490FEffa212faC2f6553682C219E6a8845' \
  -H "x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY"
```

## Response (200)

Success: get the attribution calldata suffix for your API key

Response headers: `x-ratelimit-limit`, `x-ratelimit-remaining`, `x-ratelimit-reset` (see [Errors, rate limits and retries](/api-reference/errors)).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| - | - | - | - |
| `suffix` | string, pattern `^[0-9a-fA-F]+$` | yes | Hex attribution suffix without 0x prefix. v2 vault-call calldata already ends with it (approve calls are not suffixed); native value-only deposits have no calldata or suffix. Append it to calldata only if you build transactions yourself. |

Example (Real response captured 2026-10-23; arrays trimmed to 2 items): `GET /v2/transactions/suffix/0xd8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA96045/0xbeeff2490FEffa212faC2f6553682C219E6a8845`

```json

  "suffix": "232c5f404de80be3c7ef2001de2d09ce535a2a0fffc69deb"
}
```

## Errors

# Near real-time (NRT): live vault share price, assets and supply
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/nrt

> Index of the v2 NRT endpoints that read a vault's share price, total assets, total supply and underlying price live from chain, with units per field and links to every endpoint page.

This section lists the v2 near-real-time (NRT) endpoints. They read vault state from chain instead of from the hourly index. Use them when you need the current share price or totals, for example for deposit previews or live dashboards.

All requests go to `https://api.vaults.fyi` with the header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. NRT endpoints need an API key; they are not offered over x402.

## Endpoints

| Endpoint | Use it when | Required inputs | Credits |
| - | - | - | - |
| [`GET /v2/nrt/vault/{network}/{vaultId}`](/api-reference/nrt/get-vault-nrt-data) | Read share price, total assets, total supply and underlying price in one call, live from chain (e.g. deposit previews). | Path: `network`, `vaultId` | 1 |
| [`GET /v2/nrt/vault/{network}/{vaultId}/sharePrice`](/api-reference/nrt/get-vault-nrt-share-price) | Read only the live `sharePrice` (underlying assets per one whole share, a number). | Path: `network`, `vaultId` | 1 |
| [`GET /v2/nrt/vault/{network}/{vaultId}/totalSupply`](/api-reference/nrt/get-vault-nrt-total-supply) | Read only the live `totalSupply` of vault shares (integer string in LP-token base units, usually 18 decimals). | Path: `network`, `vaultId` | 1 |
| [`GET /v2/nrt/vault/{network}/{vaultId}/totalAssets`](/api-reference/nrt/get-vault-nrt-total-assets) | Read only the live `totalAssets` held by the vault (integer string in underlying-asset base units). | Path: `network`, `vaultId` | 1 |
| [`GET /v2/nrt/vault/{network}/{vaultId}/underlyingAssetPrice`](/api-reference/nrt/get-vault-nrt-underlying-asset-price) | Read only the live USD price of one whole underlying token (a number, unlike `assetPriceInUsd` strings elsewhere). | Path: `network`, `vaultId` | 1 |

Each NRT call costs 1 credit and needs an API key; NRT is not available over [x402](/ai-agents/x402). Requests that don't return 200 are not charged.

## Units

| Field | Type | Unit |
| - | - | - |
| `sharePrice` | number | Underlying assets per one whole share (e.g. `1.0139`) |
| `totalSupply` | integer string | Vault shares in **LP-token** base units (usually 18 decimals), not asset units |
| `totalAssets` | integer string | Underlying asset in its base units (USDC: 6 decimals) |
| `underlyingAssetPrice` | number | USD per one whole underlying token. Elsewhere, prices are strings (`assetPriceInUsd`). |

## Example

```bash
curl -H "x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY" \
  "https://api.vaults.fyi/v2/nrt/vault/base/0xbeeff2490FEffa212faC2f6553682C219E6a8845"
```

Response, captured 2026-10-23 (complete):

```json
{
  "totalSupply": "461739224418397752974334633",
  "totalAssets": "468178256927439",
  "sharePrice": 1.013945135111877,
  "underlyingAssetPrice": 0.99985668
}
```

`totalAssets` / 10^6 = 468,178,256.93 USDC. `totalSupply` / 10^18 = 461,739,224.42 shares. Their ratio matches `sharePrice`.

Values are read from the chain's latest block when you call the endpoint, with no response cache, so they are typically at most a block or a second old. `sharePrice` is the amount of underlying asset per one whole share, adjusted for decimals. `totalSupply` is in share-token base units: use the share token's decimals, not the asset's. NRT returns no APY.

## Related beta endpoints

| Endpoint | Use it when | Status | Credits |
| - | - | - | - |
| [`GET /beta/borrow/markets/nrt/{network}/{marketId}/{assetId}`](/api-reference/borrow-markets/get-borrow-market-asset-nrt-data) | Live rates and liquidity for one asset in a market. `assetId` = `assetsData[].marketAssetId`. | Beta | 1 |

Related: [Historical](/api-reference/historical) (indexed time series), [Conventions](/api-reference/conventions), [Errors](/api-reference/errors).


# Get live on-chain share price, supply and assets of a vault
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/nrt/get-vault-nrt-data

> Returns near-real-time vault state read from the chain's latest block at request time (no response cache, so values are typically at most a block or a second old): `totalSupply` (vault shares in the share token's base units, usually 18 decimals; use the share token's decimals, not the asset's), `totalAssets` (underlying-asset base units), `sharePrice` (underlying assets per one whole share, a float) and `underlyingAssetPrice` (USD per whole underlying token, a number). Use BigInt or decimal-safe division for totalAssets / totalSupply with each token's own decimals; do not convert these integer strings to JavaScript Number before scaling. Use for deposit previews; use the single-field variants to fetch one value. /v2/nrt/* needs an API key: NRT is not sold over x402. Cost: 1 credit. Docs: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/nrt/get-vault-nrt-data.

## Request

`GET https://api.vaults.fyi/v2/nrt/vault/{network}/{vaultId}`

- Auth: header `x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY`. This endpoint needs an API key; an invalid key returns 401.
- Credits: 1 credit ([Credits](/plans/credits)).
- Stability: stable (v2) ([Versioning](/api-reference/versioning)).
- operationId: `getVaultNrt`. Section: [Nrt](/api-reference/nrt).

## Parameters

| Name | In | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| `network` | path | string: one of 44 values (`mainnet`, `optimism`, `arbitrum`, …; full list in the OpenAPI block) | yes | — | Network name (e.g. `base`, `mainnet`) or CAIP-2 ID (e.g. `eip155:8453`). Bare chain IDs (`8453`) and `ethereum` are rejected with 400. List all with GET /v2/networks. |
| `vaultId` | path | string | yes | — | Vault identifier: `vaultId` from GET /v2/vaults or /v2/detailed-vaults, an opaque string. Either the vault contract address, or `<address>-<descriptor>` for vaults that share one contract (e.g. `0x559756d476D5ed4533edC3Ac98E5A9468176378c-25`): copy it, don't derive it from `address`. The address part is case-insensitive; pass the descriptor exactly as returned. A vault that migrates to a new contract gets a new vaultId. Must belong to `{network}`; otherwise 400 'Vault ... on network ... not found'. Non-vault strings return 400 'not a valid vault id'. |

## Example request


## Response (200)

Success: get live on-chain share price, supply and assets of a vault

Response headers: `x-ratelimit-limit`, `x-ratelimit-remaining`, `x-ratelimit-reset` (see [Errors, rate limits and retries](/api-reference/errors)).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| - | - | - | - |
| `totalSupply` | string | yes | Total vault shares outstanding, integer string in the share (LP) token's base units, not asset base units (usually 18 decimals; divide by 10^lpToken.decimals). |
| `totalAssets` | string | yes | Total underlying assets held by the vault, integer string in asset base units (divide by 10^asset.decimals). |
| `sharePrice` | number | yes | Underlying assets per one whole vault share (float ratio, not base units). |
| `underlyingAssetPrice` | number | yes | USD price of one whole underlying token, as a JSON number (not a string). |

# Health: public API liveness check
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/api-reference/health

> Index of the public v2 health endpoint: no API key, free, not rate limited, no rate-limit headers; returns {"status":"Success"} when the API is up. It does not validate your key.

This section has one endpoint: a public liveness check for uptime monitoring. Unlike every other endpoint, it needs no API key and costs nothing.

## Endpoints

| Endpoint | Use it when | Required inputs | Credits |
| - | - | - | - |
| [`GET /v2/health`](/api-reference/health/health-check) | Liveness check. No API key needed; returns `{"status":"Success","message":"Application is healthy"}`. Does not validate your key. | None | 0 (free) |

## Things to know

- `GET /v2/health` returns 200 with or without a key, and with an invalid key. It doesn't tell you whether your key works. To check a key, call `GET /v2/networks` (1 credit): 200 means the key is valid, 401 means it is invalid, and 402 means no key was sent.
- It is free and exempt from rate limiting, so the response carries no `x-ratelimit-*` headers.
- Only `GET` is supported. `POST /v2/health` returns a route 404, not 405.

## Example

```bash
curl "https://api.vaults.fyi/v2/health"
```

Response, captured 2026-10-23 (complete):

```json
{ "status": "Success", "message": "Application is healthy" }
```

Related: [API overview](/api-reference/overview), [Errors](/api-reference/errors).

# AI agents: what you can build with vaults.fyi and which surface to use
Source: https://docs.vaults.fyi/ai-agents/overview

> What an AI agent can do with vaults.fyi (discover vaults, read positions, build unsigned transactions) and when to use the REST API, SDK, MCP server, x402 pay-per-request or llms.txt.

This page answers two questions: what an AI agent can do with vaults.fyi, and which access surface to use for each job (REST API, SDK, API MCP server, x402 pay-per-request, Docs MCP, llms.txt). Read it before you wire vaults.fyi into an agent. Then read [Rules for agents](/ai-agents/rules-for-agents), a compact rule list to paste into the agent's context, and [Transaction safety](/ai-agents/transaction-safety) if the agent builds transactions.

Facts every surface depends on:

- **REST API:** base URL `https://api.vaults.fyi`, paths start with `/v2`, `/beta` or `/alpha`. Send the key as **`x-api-key: <key>`**. Get a key at [portal.vaults.fyi/signup](https://portal.vaults.fyi/signup).
- **MCP server:** `https://mcp.vaults.fyi/mcp`. It takes the same key, but as **`Authorization: Bearer <key>`**. A Bearer header sent to the REST API is ignored, so the request counts as keyless.
- **No key on a v2 REST endpoint** returns **HTTP 402** with an x402 payment challenge, not 401. Pay per request ([x402](/ai-agents/x402)) or add `x-api-key`.
- **Transactions are unsigned.** vaults.fyi returns calldata. It never signs, never broadcasts, never checks the wallet balance and does not simulate. Your agent verifies each transaction, a human confirms it, and the user's wallet signs it.

## What an agent can do

| Job | REST endpoint (v2) | MCP tool | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Find and rank vaults | `GET /v2/detailed-vaults` | `vaults_search` | Defaults to 4 networks (`base`, `mainnet`, `arbitrum`, `optimism`) and `minTvl` 100000 USD. Sort ascending by default: send `sortOrder=desc` to rank. |
| One vault's APY, TVL, score, warnings | `GET /v2/detailed-vaults/{network}/{vaultId}` | `vault_details` | APY is a decimal fraction: `0.0551` = 5.51%, net of fees. |
| Compare with a market rate | `GET /v2/benchmarks/{network}?code=usd` (or `eth`) | `benchmark_apy` | Read `apy.<window>.total`. |
| History (APY, TVL, share price) | `GET /v2/historical/{network}/{vaultId}` and `/apy`, `/tvl`, `/sharePrice` | `vault_history`, `vault_apy_history`, … | REST takes Unix seconds; MCP takes ISO 8601 strings. Oldest point first. |
| A wallet's vault positions | `GET /v2/portfolio/positions/{userAddress}` | `positions` | Position size is `asset.positionValueInAsset` or `lpToken.balanceUsd`. `asset.balanceNative`/`balanceUsd` is the wallet's **idle** balance of the underlying token. |
| A wallet's idle tokens and deposit ideas | `GET /v2/portfolio/idle-assets/{userAddress}`, `GET /v2/portfolio/best-deposit-options/{userAddress}` | `wallet_balances`, `best_deposit_options` | Results include non-transactional options. Filter them out. |
| Deposit or withdraw | `GET /v2/transactions/context/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}`, then `GET /v2/transactions/{action}/{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}` | `transaction_context`, then `build_vault_tx` | `userAddress` comes **before** `network`. Amounts are base-unit integer strings (`1000000` = 1 USDC). |
| Queued (async) withdrawals | same two endpoints with `action` `request-redeem`, later `claim-redeem` | same tools | Read `currentRedeemStep` and `pendingRequests` from the context to know the next action. The API does not abstract the waiting. |
| Claim Merkl rewards | `GET /v2/transactions/rewards/context/{userAddress}`, then `GET /v2/transactions/rewards/claim/{userAddress}?claimIds=<id>&claimIds=<id>` | `rewards`, then `build_claim_rewards` (one call per network) | Take `claimId` values from `claimable.<network>[]`. |
| Solana vaults | `/beta/svm/*` (Beta) | none | Not on MCP and not on x402. |

What vaults.fyi does **not** do for the agent:

- **It does not assess risk for you.** The Reputation Score is `score.vaultScore` (0 to 100; observed 27.5–99.1 in live data on 2026-10-23). It is not a risk rating, and there are no risk tiers. If you need a strict score threshold, check `score.vaultScore` client-side, and drop vaults with non-empty `warnings` or `flags`, `isCorrupted: true` or `isTransactional: false`.
- **It does not check whether the transaction will succeed.** A deposit payload is returned even if the wallet's balance is too low. Check both yourself and simulate before signing ([Transaction safety](/ai-agents/transaction-safety)).
- **It does not choose for the user.** Recommendation endpoints (`best-vault`, `best-deposit-options`) are suggestions. `best-vault` picks, per asset the wallet holds, the vault with the highest total APY for `apyInterval` (default `7day`) among featured vaults without warnings, then returns the asset/vault pair with the highest projected annual earnings. It does not filter on `isTransactional`; pass `onlyTransactional=true` if you will build a deposit.

## Which surface to use

| Surface | Use it when | Auth | Entry point |
|---|---|---|---|
| **REST API** | You write code (backend, script, agent tool) and want every endpoint, including Beta and Alpha | `x-api-key: <key>` | [API overview](/api-reference/overview), [Conventions](/api-reference/conventions), OpenAPI: `https://api.vaults.fyi/v2/documentation/json` (also `/beta/documentation/json`, `/alpha/documentation/json`) |
| **SDK** | You write TypeScript or Python and want typed wrappers over the REST API | API key | `npm install @vaultsfyi/sdk`, `pip install vaultsfyi`. See [SDK quickstart](/sdk/quickstart) |
| **API MCP server** | An MCP client (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor) should query live data or build unsigned transactions in conversation | `Authorization: Bearer <key>` | `https://mcp.vaults.fyi/mcp`. See [MCP server](/ai-agents/mcp-server) |
| **x402 pay-per-request** | An autonomous agent has a Base wallet with USDC and no API key | None. It pays USDC on Base per request | Any v2 REST endpoint without `x-api-key`. See [x402](/ai-agents/x402) |
| **Docs MCP** | An MCP client should search and read these docs and the OpenAPI specs | None | `https://docs.vaults.fyi/mcp` (tools `search_vaults_fyi`, `query_docs_filesystem_vaults_fyi`) |
| **llms.txt / Markdown pages** | An LLM should read the docs directly | None | `https://docs.vaults.fyi/llms.txt` (index), `https://docs.vaults.fyi/llms-full.txt` (everything). Every page is also available as Markdown at `<page URL>.md` |

How to choose:

- **The agent writes integration code** → REST API (or SDK) for the code, plus the Docs MCP or `llms.txt` to read docs. Copy endpoint paths from the OpenAPI spec, not from memory.
- **The agent answers questions or prepares transactions in chat** → API MCP server. Its tools return JSON inside `result.content[0].text`; parse it.
- **The agent has no API key and pays its own way** → x402 on the REST API. MCP needs a key and has no x402 option.
- **You need Solana, Beta or Alpha endpoints** → REST API with a key. Beta, Alpha and NRT (`/v2/nrt/*`) endpoints need an API key: they are not offered over x402. The MCP server has no tools for them.

### The two `llms.txt` files

Use `https://docs.vaults.fyi/llms.txt`, the index of this site, rather than other copies such as `https://api.vaults.fyi/llms.txt`.

## Start small: three first calls

Costs are in credits (CU). Pay-as-you-go is $0.002 per credit ([Credits](/plans/credits)).

1. **Data only** (1 + 3 CU per vault returned):

   ```bash
   curl -sS "https://api.vaults.fyi/v2/detailed-vaults?allowedNetworks=base&allowedAssets=USDC&minTvl=10000000&sortBy=apy7day&sortOrder=desc&perPage=5" \
     -H "x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY"
   ```

2. **Transaction context, then payload** (3 CU + 5 CU). The path order is `{userAddress}/{network}/{vaultId}`:

   ```bash
   curl -sS "https://api.vaults.fyi/v2/transactions/context/0xd8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA96045/base/0xbeeff2490FEffa212faC2f6553682C219E6a8845" \
     -H "x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY"
   curl -sS "https://api.vaults.fyi/v2/transactions/deposit/0xd8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA96045/base/0xbeeff2490FEffa212faC2f6553682C219E6a8845?assetAddress=0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913&amount=1000000" \
     -H "x-api-key: $VAULTSFYI_API_KEY"
   ```

   The response is `{currentActionIndex, actions[]}`, each action being `{name, tx: {to, chainId, data, value?}}`. Verify, confirm and sign in order ([Transaction safety](/ai-agents/transaction-safety)).

3. **Keyless:** the same `GET /v2/networks` without `x-api-key` returns 402 with a price of `"2000"` ($0.002 in USDC base units) ([x402](/ai-agents/x402)).
